# Code Setup & package read in

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r read in packages}
library(vegan)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)
library(iNEXT) # species diversity
library(hillR) # species diversity
```

# Read in and prep data

## Read in

```{r data read in}
all_surv_records <- read.csv("Data/all_survey_records_aug2026.csv")
# a record of every segment surveyed, afternoon and night, with length and time

amph_lz <- read.csv("Data/amph_lz_cleaned_aug2026.csv")
# cleaned amphibian and lizard data - a record of every individual found, when, and what segment
# make sure there are no duplicates...
amph_lz <- amph_lz %>%
  distinct(Animal_ID, .keep_all = TRUE) # evidently there was 1

# I cleaned frogs and added a tadpole phase column, now they are a sep df
frogs_df <- read.csv("frogs.csv")
frogs_df$Start_Date <- mdy(frogs_df$Start_Date)

effort <- read.csv("Data/effort_aug2026.csv")
# Date, effort hours, segment length

env_2025 <- read.csv("Data/env_2025_cleaned.csv", encoding = "latin1")
# 2025 env data

env_24_25_nights <- read.csv("Data/env_24_25_nights_aug2026.csv")
# night time survey environmental data both years

small.mamms.df <- read.csv("Data/small_mammals_aug2026.csv")
# records of small mammals spotted during surveys

snakes.master <- read.csv("Data/snakes_master_cleaned_aug2026.csv")
# all snake records

snakes.sur <- read.csv("Data/snake_surveys_cleaned_aug2026.csv")
# all the snake survey records, cleaned
# this version of snakes.sur has those two duplicates (SK04, 05) removed

```

# Prep env data

```{r prep env and join to obs dfs}

humidity_long <- env_2025 %>%
  filter(Survey_Type == "Night") %>%
  select(Date, Station, 
         Humidity_1:Humidity_8, Humidity_Final) %>%
  pivot_longer(names_to = "Measurement",
               cols = Humidity_1:Humidity_Final,
               values_to = "Humidity", names_repair = "unique")
# remove NAs
humidity_long <- humidity_long %>%
  na.omit()

# fix date
humidity_long$Start_Date <- mdy(humidity_long$Date)

humidity_long <- humidity_long %>%
  select(-Date)
# there are 3 humidity readings that are very low (<70) and are all the 1 (or 2nd) reading of the night - this could be error, and our sampling intensity is robust enough for us to not worry about influencing results by removing these outliers. 

humidity_long <- humidity_long %>%
  filter(Humidity > 70)

# repeat with temp
temp_long <- env_2025 %>%
  filter(Survey_Type == "Night") %>%
  select(Date, Station, 
         Temperature_1:Temperature_8, Temperature_Final) %>%
  pivot_longer(names_to = "Measurement",
               cols = Temperature_1:Temperature_Final,
               values_to = "Temperature", names_repair = "unique")

# remove NAs
temp_long <- temp_long %>%
  na.omit()

# date
temp_long$Start_Date <- mdy(temp_long$Date)
temp_long <- temp_long %>%
  select(-Date)


# 2024 data

# pull out 2024 year only
env_24_25_nights$Start_Date <- ymd(env_24_25_nights$Start_Date)
env_24_25_nights$Year<- factor(format(env_24_25_nights$Start_Date, "%Y"))
  
env_2024 <- env_24_25_nights %>%
  filter(Year == "2024")

# humidity - 2024 - pivot

# simplify
env_2024 <- env_2024 %>%
  select(-Effort_hrs, -Notes, -Number_of_Small_Mammals_Spotted, -Number_of_Water_Bodies_Spotted, -Surveyors, -Searching_Time, -Meters, -Order, -Survey_Start_Time, -Survey_End_Time)

humidity_long_2024 <- env_2024 %>%
  select(Start_Date, Station,
         Humidity_1:Humidity_8, Humidity_Final) %>%
  pivot_longer(names_to = "Measurement",
               cols = Humidity_1:Humidity_Final,
               values_to = "Humidity", names_repair = "unique")
# remove NAs

humidity_long_2024 <- humidity_long_2024 %>%
  na.omit()

# repeat with temp
temperature_long_2024 <- env_2024 %>%
  select(Start_Date, Station,
         Temperature_1:Temperature_8, Temperature_Final) %>%
  pivot_longer(names_to = "Measurement",
               cols = Temperature_1:Temperature_Final,
               values_to = "Temperature", names_repair = "unique")
# remove NAs

temperature_long_2024 <- temperature_long_2024 %>%
  na.omit()

# join
humidity_all <- rbind(humidity_long, humidity_long_2024)
temperature_all <- rbind(temp_long, temperature_long_2024)

# get means
humidity_means <- humidity_all %>%
  group_by(Station, Start_Date) %>%
  reframe(mean_relative_humidity = mean(Humidity))

temperature_means <- temperature_all %>%
  group_by(Station, Start_Date) %>%
  reframe(mean_temp_F = mean(Temperature))

# center and scale
humidity_means$humidity_scaled <-scale(humidity_means$mean_relative_humidity)

temperature_means$temp_scaled <-scale(temperature_means$mean_temp_F)

# understory not included in models so not bothering with it here

# clean 
rm(humidity_all, humidity_long, humidity_long_2024, temp_long, temperature_all, temperature_long_2024, env_2024, env_2025, env_24_25_nights)

```

# Prep snake data

```{r add bins}

snakes.sur <- snakes.sur %>%
  mutate(Dist_bin_mammal_eaters = ifelse(Distance_From_Trail_m <= 0.75, "0_0.75", NA))

snakes.sur <- snakes.sur %>%
  mutate(Dist_bin_mammal_eaters = ifelse(Distance_From_Trail_m > 0.75 & Distance_From_Trail_m <= 1.75, "0.75_1.75", Dist_bin_mammal_eaters))

snakes.sur <- snakes.sur %>%
  mutate(Dist_bin_mammal_eaters = ifelse(Distance_From_Trail_m > 1.75 & Distance_From_Trail_m <= 2.5, "1.75_2.5", Dist_bin_mammal_eaters))

snakes.sur <- snakes.sur %>%
  mutate(Dist_bin_mammal_eaters = ifelse(Distance_From_Trail_m > 2.5 & Distance_From_Trail_m <= 3.5, "2.5_3.5", Dist_bin_mammal_eaters))

snakes.sur <- snakes.sur %>%
  mutate(Dist_bin_mammal_eaters = ifelse(Distance_From_Trail_m > 3.5 & Distance_From_Trail_m <= 5, "3.5_5", Dist_bin_mammal_eaters))

snakes.sur <- snakes.sur %>%
  mutate(Dist_bin_mammal_eaters = ifelse(Distance_From_Trail_m > 5, "5_8", Dist_bin_mammal_eaters))

# v 2 for non_mammal_eaters
snakes.sur <- snakes.sur %>%
  mutate(Dist_bin_no_mams = ifelse(Distance_From_Trail_m <= 1.25, "0_1.25", NA))

snakes.sur <- snakes.sur %>%
  mutate(Dist_bin_no_mams = ifelse(Distance_From_Trail_m > 1.25 & Distance_From_Trail_m <= 2.5, "1.25_2.5", Dist_bin_no_mams))

snakes.sur <- snakes.sur %>%
  mutate(Dist_bin_no_mams = ifelse(Distance_From_Trail_m > 2.5 & Distance_From_Trail_m <= 3.5, "2.5_3.5", Dist_bin_no_mams))

snakes.sur <- snakes.sur %>%
  mutate(Dist_bin_no_mams = ifelse(Distance_From_Trail_m > 3.5 & Distance_From_Trail_m <= 4.5, "3.5_4.5", Dist_bin_no_mams))

snakes.sur <- snakes.sur %>%
  mutate(Dist_bin_no_mams = ifelse(Distance_From_Trail_m > 4.5 & Distance_From_Trail_m <= 6, "4.5_6", Dist_bin_no_mams))

```

```{r prep snake data 2 diet types}

# make one data frame of only the snake records (remove NAs where no snakes were found) 
surveys_with_snakes <- snakes.sur %>% filter(!is.na(Snake_ID))

# likewise, make one df of only cases where no snakes were found and keep relevant columns with it
surveys_without_snakes <- snakes.sur %>% filter(is.na(Snake_ID)) %>%
  select(Start_Date, Station, Segment, Seg_dist_m, Dist_bin_no_mams, Dist_bin_mammal_eaters)

# get counts of n snakes found per diet type per segment per survey
n_snakes_per_guild <- surveys_with_snakes %>%
  group_by(Start_Date, Station, Diet_Type, Segment, Seg_dist_m, Dist_bin_no_mams, Dist_bin_mammal_eaters) %>%
  reframe(n_snakes = n()) 

# account for cases when no snakes for a given guild were found on a segment
# this is step 1 of accounting for cases where a snake in a given guild wasn't found on a segment and needs to be noted with a zero
n_snakes_per_guild <- n_snakes_per_guild %>% 
  complete(Diet_Type, nesting(Start_Date, Segment, Station, Seg_dist_m, Dist_bin_no_mams, Dist_bin_mammal_eaters), fill = list(n_snakes = 0))

# add in the instances where no snakes were found for a given survey
n_snakes_per_guild <- bind_rows(n_snakes_per_guild, surveys_without_snakes)

# and repeat the process of making sure we have a numerical record (including 0s if none were found) for each diet type for each segment
n_snakes_per_guild <-n_snakes_per_guild %>% 
  complete(Diet_Type, nesting(Start_Date, Segment, Station, Seg_dist_m, Dist_bin_no_mams, Dist_bin_mammal_eaters), fill = list(n_snakes = 0))

n_snakes_per_guild <- n_snakes_per_guild %>% na.omit

```

## Add env data to dfs

```{r add env to dfs}

# n snakes per guild
# fix date first
n_snakes_per_guild$Start_Date <- mdy(n_snakes_per_guild$Start_Date)

# add humidity
n_snakes_per_guild <- left_join(n_snakes_per_guild, humidity_means)
# and add temp
n_snakes_per_guild <- left_join(n_snakes_per_guild, temperature_means)

# drop NA where datalogger wasn't working
n_snakes_per_guild <- n_snakes_per_guild %>%
  na.omit()

```

# Density estimates

Sort of following Hierarchical distance sampling to estimate population sizes of common lizards across a desert ecoregion (in Zotero shared library)

```{r make umf two diet types}

n_snakes_per_guild$Diet_Type <- as.factor(n_snakes_per_guild$Diet_Type)
n_snakes_per_guild$Seg_dist_m <- as.numeric(n_snakes_per_guild$Seg_dist_m)
n_snakes_per_guild$Segment <- as.factor(n_snakes_per_guild$Segment)
n_snakes_per_guild$Station <- as.factor(n_snakes_per_guild$Station)

# make one dataframe for each diet type
mammal_eaters<- n_snakes_per_guild %>%
  filter(Diet_Type == "consumes_mammals")

mammal_eaters <- mammal_eaters %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Dist_bin_mammal_eaters,
              values_from = n_snakes, 
              values_fill = 0)

non_mammal_eaters <- n_snakes_per_guild %>%
  filter(Diet_Type == "no_mammals")

non_mammal_eaters <- non_mammal_eaters %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Dist_bin_no_mams,
              values_from = n_snakes, 
              values_fill = 0)

# why the fuck are the columns out of order
colnames(mammal_eaters)

non_mammal_eaters<- non_mammal_eaters[, c("Diet_Type","Start_Date","Segment","Station", "Seg_dist_m",         "humidity_scaled", "temp_scaled", "0_1.25", "1.25_2.5", "2.5_3.5", "3.5_4.5", "4.5_6")]  

mammal_eaters<- mammal_eaters[, c("Diet_Type","Start_Date","Segment","Station", "Seg_dist_m",         "humidity_scaled", "temp_scaled", "0_0.75", "0.75_1.75", "1.75_2.5", "2.5_3.5", "3.5_5", "5_8")]  

# separate out the covariates
mammal_eaters.covs <- mammal_eaters[,c("Station", "Diet_Type", "Segment", "Seg_dist_m", "humidity_scaled", "temp_scaled")]

non.mammal_eaters.covs <- non_mammal_eaters[,c("Station", "Diet_Type", "Segment", "Seg_dist_m", "humidity_scaled", "temp_scaled")]

mammal.eaters.umf <- unmarkedFrameDS(y=as.matrix(mammal_eaters[,8:ncol(mammal_eaters)]), siteCovs=data.frame(mammal_eaters.covs), dist.breaks=c(0, 0.75, 1.75, 2.5, 3.5, 5, 8), unitsIn="m", survey="line", tlength=mammal_eaters.covs$Seg_dist_m)

hist(mammal.eaters.umf, xlab="distance (m)", main="", cex.lab=0.8, cex.axis=0.8)

non.mammal.eaters.umf <- unmarkedFrameDS(y=as.matrix(non_mammal_eaters[,8:ncol(non_mammal_eaters)]), siteCovs=data.frame(non.mammal_eaters.covs), dist.breaks=c(0, 1.25, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5, 6), unitsIn="m", survey="line", tlength=non.mammal_eaters.covs$Seg_dist_m)

hist(non.mammal.eaters.umf, xlab="distance (m)", main="", cex.lab=0.8, cex.axis=0.8)

```

### GOF function

Goodness of fit tests

```{r gof function}

# using this resource: https://www.montana.edu/screel/teaching/bioe-440r-521/bioe-440-distance-sampling.html

# Goodness of fit test: good fit if results of these tests show p > 0.05. First, fit a model: use your best-supported model (Lowest AIC). Then check GOF for that model.

# Function returning three fit-statistics.

fitstats <- function(fm) {

  observed <- getY(fm@data)

  expected <- fitted(fm)

  resids <- residuals(fm)

  sse <- sum(resids^2)

  chisq <- sum((observed - expected)^2 / expected)

  freeTuke <- sum((sqrt(observed) - sqrt(expected))^2)

  out <- c(SSE=sse, Chisq=chisq, freemanTukey=freeTuke)

  return(out)

}

```

## Model Diet Types

```{r mammal eaters}

# first term is p, detection probability
# second term is density, N

null <- distsamp(~1 ~ 1, mammal.eaters.umf, unitsOut = "kmsq", keyfun = "hazard")
summary(null)

Station <- distsamp(~ 1 ~ Station, mammal.eaters.umf, unitsOut = "kmsq", keyfun = "hazard")
summary(Station)

# temp
Station_Temp <- distsamp(~ 1 ~ Station + temp_scaled, mammal.eaters.umf, unitsOut = "kmsq", keyfun = "hazard")

# humidity
Station_humidity <- distsamp(~ 1 ~ Station + humidity_scaled, mammal.eaters.umf, unitsOut = "kmsq", keyfun = "hazard")

# both
Station_Temp_Humidity <- distsamp(~ 1 ~ Station + temp_scaled + humidity_scaled, mammal.eaters.umf, unitsOut = "kmsq", keyfun = "hazard")

# Make a table to compare models

# put mods in a list
mod.set<- list(null = null, Station = Station, Station_Temp = Station_Temp, Station_humidity = Station_humidity, Station_Temp_Humidity)

# make table
aic_table <- aictab(cand.set = mod.set, sort = TRUE)

aic_table
```

### GOF

```{r goodness of fit three guilds}
pb_station_mammal_eaters <- parboot(Station, fitstats, nsim=100)
pb_station_mammal_eaters
# fine
```

```{r predicted values}

new.data <- mammal_eaters %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(Station) %>%
  distinct()
  

#Predict

predictions <- predict(Station, type="state", newdata=new.data, appendData=TRUE)

```

```{r plot guilds, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
p_mammal_eaters<-ggplot(predictions, aes(x=Station, y=Predicted)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Predicted - SE, ymax = Predicted + SE), width = .2) + geom_point(size = 2) + theme_pubclean() + scale_fill_manual(values = c("goldenrod1", "gray")) + xlab("") + scale_color_discrete(labels = "") +  scale_y_continuous(name = expression(bold(paste("Snakes /  ", km^bold("2"))))) + ggtitle("Density estimates of mammal-eating snakes") + theme(axis.text = element_text(color = "black"))+
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Unhunted", "Hunted"))

p_mammal_eaters
```

Appears to be elevated numbers in hunted forest in the guild that is mostly mammal consumers.

## Family level

The two most detected families are Boidae and Colubridae. Limitting the analysis to these 2 families allows the models to run without error with Family as a covariate. Including all families detected creates model issues with uncertainty because the other families were only detected 1 or 2 times. 

```{r format for unmarked based on fams}

# also isolate surveys that DID have snakes detected
surveys.no.zeros <- snakes.sur %>%
  filter(!is.na(Snake_ID))

# SK04 and SK05 are duplicated
# remove the duplicate entries

surveys.no.zeros <- surveys.no.zeros %>%
  filter(!duplicated(Snake_ID))

# tally counts - df without zeros
survey.tally <- surveys.no.zeros %>%
  filter(Family != "Viperidae") %>%
filter(Family != "Elapidae") %>%
  group_by(Start_Date, Year, Station, Family, Segment, Seg_dist_m, Distance_bin_m) %>% tally()

# generate all possible combinations based on family to get zeros

df_long <- survey.tally %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  complete(Family, Distance_bin_m, nesting(Start_Date, Year, Station, Segment, Seg_dist_m), fill = list(n = 0))

# also, which families eat what?
snakes.sur %>%
  group_by(Family) %>%
  reframe(unique(Diet_Type)) # colubridae is only possibility for mixed in our data?

# pivot wider that wider
density_fam_df <- df_long %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Distance_bin_m,
              values_from = n, 
              values_fill = 0)
```

## Model family level density

```{r model at fam level}
# separate out the covariates

# model not running bc of sparse data at fam level - removed elapidae, which only had 1 detection, and Viperidae which only had 2

covs.fam <- density_fam_df[,c("Station", "Year", "Family", "Segment", "Seg_dist_m")]

umf.fam <- unmarkedFrameDS(y=as.matrix(density_fam_df[,7:ncol(density_fam_df)]), siteCovs=data.frame(covs.fam), dist.breaks=c( 0,2,4,6, 8), unitsIn="m", survey="line", tlength=covs.fam$Seg_dist_m)

# run models
# null
null.fam <- distsamp(~1 ~ 1, umf.fam, unitsOut = "kmsq", keyfun = "uniform")
summary(null.fam)

# family as detection covariate, no density covariate
fam.null  <- distsamp(~Family ~ 1, umf.fam, unitsOut = "kmsq",keyfun = "uniform")
summary(fam.null)

# add year as density covariate
year <- distsamp(~ 1 ~ Year, umf.fam, unitsOut = "kmsq", keyfun = "uniform")
summary(year)

# add station as density covariate
station <- distsamp(~1 ~ Station, umf.fam, unitsOut = "kmsq", keyfun = "uniform")
summary(station)

# add station and station x family interaction term 

station_stationXfam <- distsamp(~1 ~ Station/Family, umf.fam, unitsOut = "kmsq", keyfun = "uniform")

summary(station_stationXfam)
# best mod by far

# put mods in a list
mod.set.family <- list(null.fam = null.fam, fam.null = fam.null, year = year, station = station, station_stationXfam = station_stationXfam)

# make table
aic_table.fam <- aictab(cand.set = mod.set.family, sort = TRUE)

aic_table.fam
```

## Predicted vals fam

```{r predicted values three guilds}

new.data.fam <- density_fam_df %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(Station, Family) %>%

predictions.fam <- predict(station_stationXfam, type="state", newdata=new.data.fam, appendData=TRUE)

```
